slides.teacher_cue: What sound?
slides.expected_response: Students respond /s/ quickly and cleanly.
slides.correction_move: Model /s/, students repeat three times, then recheck.
slides.observation_note: Watch for /sh/ drift and delayed retrieval.

slides.teacher_cue: What sound?
slides.expected_response: Students respond /a/ quickly and cleanly.
slides.correction_move: Model /a/, students repeat three times, then recheck.
slides.observation_note: Watch for uncertain retrieval and drifting vowel quality.

slides.teacher_cue: What sound?
slides.expected_response: Students respond /t/ quickly and cleanly.
slides.correction_move: Model /t/, students repeat three times, then recheck.
slides.observation_note: Watch for weak release or delayed retrieval.

slides.teacher_cue: Play sat once, then replay only if needed before checking.
slides.expected_response: Students write sat accurately on paper or a whiteboard.
slides.correction_move: Replay sat once, then segment /s/ /a/ /t/ orally before checking.
slides.observation_note: Watch whether students can still hold the full word from sound to print.

slides.teacher_cue: Play at once, then replay only if needed before checking.
slides.expected_response: Students write at accurately on paper or a whiteboard.
slides.correction_move: Replay at once, then segment /a/ /t/ orally before checking.
slides.observation_note: Watch whether students can encode a shorter word without adding extra sounds.

slides.teacher_cue: Play as once, then replay only if needed before checking.
slides.expected_response: Students write as accurately on paper or a whiteboard.
slides.correction_move: Replay as once, then segment /a/ /s/ orally before checking.
slides.observation_note: Watch whether students can hear the final /s/ clearly in a short word.

slides.teacher_cue: New sound today. Keep it short, relaxed, and quick.
slides.expected_response: Students produce short /ɪ/ cleanly without stretching it.
slides.correction_move: Model a short relaxed /ɪ/, contrast it with a longer /iː/, then repeat.
slides.observation_note: Watch for tense, overlong vowel production and confusion with /iː/.

slides.teacher_cue: Model sit with the action first, then reveal the written word.
slides.expected_response: Students say sit orally and connect it to the action before print.
slides.correction_move: Model sit, gesture the action again, then repeat and reveal the word.
slides.observation_note: Watch whether students hold the short i sound in a known action word.

slides.teacher_cue: Teach it as a whole-word sight word in a simple oral question, then reveal print.
slides.expected_response: Students say it orally in context and recognise it as a high-frequency word.
slides.correction_move: Model the full word it in a short sentence, then repeat and reveal the word.
slides.observation_note: Watch whether students treat it as a whole useful word, not just isolated sounds.

slides.teacher_cue: Use a short possessive phrase orally, then reveal the written word its.
slides.expected_response: Students say its orally and connect it to ownership meaning before print.
slides.correction_move: Model its in a short phrase, point to the owned object, then repeat and reveal.
slides.observation_note: Watch whether students can hold the full word and final /s/ in connected speech.

slides.teacher_cue: Teach is as a whole-word sight word in a short oral sentence, then reveal print.
slides.expected_response: Students say is orally in context and recognise it as a high-frequency word.
slides.correction_move: Model is in a short sentence, then repeat chorally and reveal the word.
slides.observation_note: Watch whether students can use is orally before seeing the written form.

slides.teacher_cue: Say the sounds and build left to right.
slides.expected_response: Students build sit using the new short i vowel.
slides.correction_move: Return to oral segmenting, then rebuild one sound at a time.
slides.observation_note: Watch whether students can hold the new vowel in the middle of the word.

slides.teacher_cue: Build the word you hear from left to right.
slides.expected_response: Students build it accurately as i | t.
slides.correction_move: Repeat the word orally, isolate each sound, then rebuild.
slides.observation_note: Watch whether students can map a short high-frequency word accurately.

slides.teacher_cue: Build the word and keep the final sound at the end.
slides.expected_response: Students build its accurately as i | t | s.
slides.correction_move: Return to oral segmenting, then rebuild one sound at a time from the start.
slides.observation_note: Watch whether students preserve all three sounds, especially the final /s/.

slides.teacher_cue: Track left to right and read the full sentence.
slides.expected_response: Students read I sit. accurately.
slides.correction_move: Model the sentence once, then return to one-to-one tracking.
slides.observation_note: Watch whether students can hold the new vowel inside a simple sentence.

slides.teacher_cue: Track left to right and read the full sentence.
slides.expected_response: Students read It sat. accurately.
slides.correction_move: Model the sentence once, then return to one-to-one tracking.
slides.observation_note: Watch whether students can keep the sight word it and the decodable word sat separate.

slides.teacher_cue: Read both sentences and notice the change from sit to sat.
slides.expected_response: Students read both sentences and notice the vowel contrast.
slides.correction_move: Model both sentences, then isolate sit and sat before rereading.
slides.observation_note: Watch whether students can compare the two similar words inside connected reading.

content_payload.comprehension_prompt: Which word says sit? Which says sat? What is different?

slides.teacher_cue: Point to each word as you read, then reread for fluency.
slides.expected_response: Students read the three sentences accurately and notice the sit/sat contrast.
slides.correction_move: Echo read first, then support line by line before rereading the full passage.
slides.observation_note: Watch whether students can track each word and distinguish sit from sat in context.

slides.teacher_cue: Dictate sit once, replay once if needed, then check.
slides.expected_response: Students write sit accurately using the short i vowel.
slides.correction_move: Repeat the word, segment the sounds orally, then rewrite.
slides.observation_note: Watch whether students can encode the new vowel in writing.

slides.teacher_cue: Dictate it once, replay once if needed, then check.
slides.expected_response: Students write it accurately.
slides.correction_move: Repeat the word, segment the sounds orally, then rewrite.
slides.observation_note: Watch whether students can encode a short high-frequency word accurately.

slides.teacher_cue: Dictate its once, replay once if needed, then check.
slides.expected_response: Students write its accurately.
slides.correction_move: Repeat the word, segment the sounds orally, then rewrite.
slides.observation_note: Watch whether students preserve the final /s/ when encoding.

content_payload.comprehension_prompt: What changed? Which sound is different?

slides.teacher_cue: Read sit and sat, then ask what changed in the middle.
slides.expected_response: Students identify that the vowel changed from /ɪ/ to /a/.
slides.correction_move: Model both words, isolate the middle vowel in each, then repeat.
slides.observation_note: Watch whether students can hear that one vowel swap changes the word.

check_items.label: We have four sounds now: s, a, t, i. Which new sound did we learn today?
Can you think of a word with the i sound?

slides.teacher_cue: Close with recall, vowel contrast, and confidence.
slides.expected_response: Students answer orally and show lesson recall with the new short i sound.
slides.correction_move: Prompt with the new sound or model a full answer, then repeat.
slides.observation_note: Watch whether students can explain the sit/sat contrast and recall the new sound.
